The main takeaway from our work is that
CMNTZs can deliver a conservation benefit that is comparable to that of government-run no take zones, even when they are smaller and more numerous, and when the fishery is highly targeted.
community-managed no-take zones can provide a conservation benefit that is comparable with that provided by government-managed no-takes zones, but the latter are much more expensive to establish.

community-managed no-take zones can be an important tool for the conservation of marine biodiversity in developing tropical countries, even in situations where there is high fishing pressure and human dependence on marine resources.
